decisive_items: peripheral early ring enhancement in the arterial phase and heterogeneous internal enhancement in the delayed phase
the lesion remained hypointense in the hepatobiliary phase
no radiotracer accumulation in any of the hepatic lesions
response.rationale: Multiple well-defined hypervascular hepatic masses with high ADC and absent FDG uptake favor a benign hepatocellular lesion. Hypointensity on hepatobiliary phase excludes FNH, while peripheral early ring enhancement with heterogeneous delayed enhancement and no pooling is characteristic of inflammatory hepatocellular adenoma rather than hemangioma, HCC, metastasis, or cholangiocarcinoma.

rejected.why: FNH would typically be iso/hyperintense on hepatobiliary phase, not hypointense.
General hepatocellular adenoma lacks the peripheral ring and delayed heterogeneous enhancement pattern; inflammatory subtype is more specific.
Metastasis would usually show restricted diffusion/low ADC and often FDG avidity; high ADC and no FDG uptake argue against.
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is usually FDG avid, often CA19-9 elevated, and typically single; no FDG and normal CA19-9 argue against.
Metastatic disease is unlikely given no primary lesion, high ADC, and absent FDG uptake.
Hemangioma would show peripheral nodular enhancement and delayed pooling; the vignette explicitly notes no pooling and a ring-like enhancement pattern.
HCC would typically show arterial hyperenhancement with washout, restricted diffusion, and often tumor marker elevation; these are absent.
